arms.name: last_week
arms.description: Same settlement period 7 days earlier.

arms.name: neso_logged
arms.description: NESO's own forward carbon forecast, as recorded by the daily logger, latest snapshot before the cutoff.
arms.note: Only exists for days the logger has run (from 2026-09-30); see DATA_ISSUES X-3.

arms.name: price_da
arms.description: The known day-ahead auction price used directly as the forecast of the realised price.

arms.name: price_da_basis7d
arms.description: Day-ahead price plus the trailing 7-day mean gap between realised and day-ahead prices.

arms.name: price_last_week
arms.description: Realised price for the same period 7 days earlier.

arms.name: price_yesterday
arms.description: Realised price for the same period yesterday where published by the cutoff, else the day before.

arms.name: yesterday
arms.description: Same settlement period yesterday where published by the 11:00 cutoff, else the day before.
arms.note: About 58% of periods use the fallback; see DATA_ISSUES X-2.

arms.name: lgbm
arms.description: LightGBM, refit every 14 days on the past only. Day-ahead carbon intensity from calendar, lagged actuals, NESO demand forecast and ECMWF weather forecasts. No price or wind features.

arms.name: lgbm_noweather
arms.description: LightGBM, refit every 14 days on the past only, with weather features removed (an ablation).

arms.name: lgbm_price
arms.description: LightGBM, refit every 14 days on the past only. The `lgbm` features plus day-ahead and realised wholesale price features.

arms.name: random_carbon
arms.description: Chance level for slot ranking: the expected overlap if the slots were chosen at random.
arms.note: Not a forecast; only appears in slot_ranking.

arms.name: random_price
arms.description: Chance level for price slot ranking: the expected overlap if the cheapest slots were chosen at random.
arms.note: Not a forecast; only appears in slot_ranking.

arms.name: lgbm_both
arms.description: Experiment: the wind forecast and the night-ordering target together.

arms.name: lgbm_night
arms.description: Experiment: trained on each slot's deviation from its 18:00-07:00 night mean, plus the `lgbm_price` night level.

arms.name: lgbm_wind
arms.description: Experiment: `lgbm_price` plus NESO's day-ahead wind forecast.
arms.note: Wind history has holes; see DATA_ISSUES WIND-1, WIND-6.

arms.name: da_basis
arms.description: Forecast-optimised charging using LightGBM carbon and day-ahead price plus 7-day basis.

arms.name: day_ahead
arms.description: Forecast-optimised charging using LightGBM carbon and the known day-ahead price.

arms.name: model
arms.description: Forecast-optimised charging using LightGBM carbon (with price features) and LightGBM price forecasts.

arms.name: naive
arms.description: Forecast-optimised charging using last week's carbon and last week's realised price.

arms.name: price_lgbm
arms.description: LightGBM, refit every 14 days on the past only. Predicts realised Market Index price minus the day-ahead price (the basis), then adds the day-ahead price back.

arms.name: neso_latest_revision
arms.description: The Carbon Intensity API's historical `forecast` field. NOT day-ahead: a near-real-time estimate. Context only, never a valid baseline.

arms.name: arrival
arms.description: Charge at full power from plug-in time until the energy is delivered.

arms.name: perfect
arms.description: Charge in the slots that turn out to be best, using the actual values. An upper bound no real system can reach.

arms.name: timer
arms.description: Charge at full power from 00:00 UK time until the energy is delivered.

- The "Historic Day Ahead Wind Forecasts" file stores one vintage per target day with its issue time.
  For 2026-05-01 onward every vintage was issued on the target day itself (median 22.8 h after the
  11:00 D-1 cutoff), so zero of 153 days (May-Sep 2026) pass the leakage gate. Earlier: 2023 126 days
  and 2025 50 days were back-filled long after delivery (issued after the target day started).
  Overall 1,012 of 1,370 days (74%) are usable. By quarter: 2024 ~99%, 2025 Q1-Q3 96-100% but Q4 50%,
  2026 Q1 80%, Q2 25%, Q3 0%; 2023 Q3 0%. Over the 2025-01 to 2026-09 test period about 65% of rows have wind.
- Handling: every vintage is stored with its true issue time; the feature builder keeps only vintages
  issued by the cutoff, so unusable days get NULL wind features (LightGBM handles this). Evaluating a
  wind feature over May-Sep 2026 therefore says nothing about wind.
- Status: partly fixable going forward: see WIND-4.

issues.title: a model trained with wind degrades badly when wind is missing at prediction time
issues.body:
- 2025-01 to 2026-09 test period, wind available on 64% of rows. Where wind WAS available the wind model beat
  the baseline by 3% (MAE 17.45 vs 18.01; shape error -5%). Where it was missing it was 16% WORSE (23.65 vs
  20.31), because the missing months (May-Sep 2026, and holes in 2023-25) were seen in training with real values.
  Net effect on the whole test period: slightly worse (19.66 vs 18.83). On the 2024 development window, where
  coverage was 99%, the gain looked like 10% (16.6 vs 18.4); the gain does not generalise at that size.
- Implication: a wind feature is only safe if it is reliably present at prediction time (live capture, WIND-4)
  or the pipeline falls back to a no-wind model on days it is missing. Not promoted into the standard models.

Now I have a clear picture. Let me summarize the key findings:

**Evaluation windows:**
- Development window: 2024-07-01 to 2024-12-31 (184 days) — this was used to choose what to test, so results here are optimistic
- Test window: 2025-01-01 to 2026-09-29 (637 days) — the honest out-of-sample evaluation

**The core problem — wind coverage:**
- Development window: 99.5% wind coverage (near-perfect)
- Test window: only 64.4% wind coverage — because NESO's "Historic Day Ahead" file had back-filled data for 2024, but from May 2026 onwards, zero days had a usable D-1 forecast (issued after the cutoff), and there were holes in 2025 Q4 and 2026 Q1-Q2 as well.
- In the development window, lgbm_wind beat lgbm_price by about 10% MAE (16.63 vs 18.43), with a positive but not fully significant gap_captured_difference, and won on 63% of nights — but since this window was used to decide what to test, I need to treat it as optimistic rather than conclusive.

On the held-out test window, the picture flips: lgbm_wind actually underperforms lgbm_price, with worse MAE (19.66 vs 18.83) and RMSE (25.48 vs 24.29), a gap_captured_difference that's essentially zero (CI straddles zero), negligible grams_saved_per_night (+0.84g), and a win rate of only 54.6%, barely better than chance. This points to the model having been trained with wind data present as the likely culprit.

Digging further, the development window had near-100% wind coverage, but the test period only has ~64% coverage, so when wind is missing at prediction time LightGBM encounters NULL features that don't match training and performs 16% worse those days, while even on days wind IS available it only edges out lgbm_price by 3% -- not enough to offset the losses. This is exactly the eval window trust issue being asked about: the dev window gave a falsely optimistic ~10% MAE improvement that didn't generalize, so the answer is no, the NESO wind forecast did not reliably improve the model.

## Short answer: No — the development window was misleading; the test window says it hurt overall.

### The eval window problem

The two available windows are very different for wind:

| Window | Period | Wind coverage | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Development | 2024-07-01 – 2024-12-31 | **99.5%** | Used to *choose* what to test — not a fair eval |
| Test | 2025-01-01 – 2026-09-29 | **64.4%** | The honest out-of-sample result |

NESO's "Historic Day Ahead" file was back-filled for 2024, giving near-perfect coverage in the dev window. From May 2026 onwards, zero days had a usable D-1 vintage (all issued after the cutoff), and Q4 2025 / Q1-Q2 2026 had significant holes too (WIND-1).

### What each window says about `lgbm_wind` vs `lgbm_price`

**Development window (misleading — do not trust):**
- MAE: 16.63 vs 18.43 → apparent **10% improvement**
- `gap_captured_difference`: +0.074 (CI: -0.019 to +0.190) — positive but CI crosses zero
- `share_of_nights_better`: 63%

**Test window (trust this):**
- MAE: **19.66 vs 18.83** → wind model is **4% worse**
- RMSE: 25.48 vs 24.29 — also worse
- `gap_captured_difference`: +0.009 (CI: -0.035 to +0.054) — indistinguishable from zero
- `grams_saved_per_night`: +0.84 g — negligible
- `share_of_nights_better`: 54.6% — barely above coin flip

### Why it degraded (WIND-6)

The model was trained mostly on periods where wind was present. When wind goes missing at prediction time in the test period (36% of half-hours), LightGBM receives NULL features outside its training distribution and is **16% worse** than `lgbm_price` on those days. Even the 64% of days *with* wind only yield a ~3% MAE gain — not enough to compensate.

### Bottom line

The dev window gain of ~10% was an artefact of near-perfect wind data coverage that does not hold in production. In the honest test window the wind feature is net harmful. This is why `lgbm_wind` was not promoted into the standard models — it's only safe if wind is reliably available at prediction time (e.g. with live capture via WIND-4), or if the pipeline falls back to a no-wind model on missing days.
